title: Purpose, license grant and basic terms
blurb: Who makes the rules, how your license is proven, and the exact meaning of space station, beacon, coordinator and RACES.

T1A01.why: The service exists to **advance skills in the technical and communication phases** of the radio art.
T1A01.trap: Contesting and mass personal communication aren't the stated purpose.

T1A02.why: The **FCC** writes and enforces the amateur rules (Part 97). The ARRL is a membership group, not a regulator.

T1A03.why: Phonetics are **encouraged** for phone IDs, never required.
T1A03.trap: Not mandatory for emergencies or foreign contacts.

T1A04.why: The FCC **emails** you a link to download your license grant.
T1A04.trap: Not postal mail, and the volunteer examiners don't send it.

T1A05.why: Your license is proven by its entry in the **FCC ULS database**.
T1A05.trap: A CSCE or an NCVEC email shows you passed, not that the FCC granted a license.

T1A06.why: HF propagation beacons sit on **10 m between 28.200 and 28.300 MHz**.
T1A06.trap: Not anywhere on 10 m, and registering with the FCC doesn't free the frequency.

T1A07.why: A space station is an amateur station **more than 50 km above** the Earth's surface.
T1A07.trap: Altitude defines it, not orbiting, crew or relaying signals.

T1A08.why: A **volunteer frequency coordinator**, recognized by local amateurs, recommends repeater and auxiliary channels.
T1A08.trap: The FCC and ITU don't assign repeater channels.

T1A09.why: The **local or regional amateurs** whose stations may be repeaters or auxiliaries select the coordinator.

T1A10.why: RACES control operators need an amateur license plus **certified enrollment in a civil defense organization**.
T1A10.trap: ARES membership and ARRL recommendations aren't the requirement.

T1A11.trap: International VHF contacts and digital third-party traffic aren't banned.
